# P28.2 — Sharing & relationship network from evidence (Round 6 / DEPTH.2)

**Spec:** `docs/tickets/P28.2__sharing-relationship-network.md` · **ADR:** ADR-099 (materialize-at-scale
posture) + ADR-101 (surface reads the materialized graph — names P28.2) · **Base:**
`devin/p28-1-entity-resolution-at-scale` · **Deferral:** D-R6.2-EDGES (opened; live-over-hosted).

## Summary

Populates the empty §12 `relationship` / access-edge layer from real claims over the resolved entity
set, so the network surface can render a **real** graph instead of fixtures. The write path was
genuinely missing — the `relationship` table had never held a row (launch computed sharing edges on
read, ADR-092). This ticket adds it, **append-only and idempotent**, by **consuming** the P08.2 §29.3
sharing-edge reconciler and the P12.2 access-path closure — never re-implementing them (SIG-ENG-035).
The hosted-over-`sig-pg` run is honestly deferred (D-R6.2-EDGES) — no fabricated hosted count.

## What changed

- **`db/` — new sqitch change `relationship_materialize`** (deploy/revert/verify + plan entry): a
  nullable `input_digest` column on `relationship` + a partial UNIQUE index (mirrors
  `resolution_materialize` / ADR-099, `claim_content_digest` / ADR-059) so the edge materializer can
  `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. Additive, back-compatible (nullable, no default).
- **`reconcile/materialize.py` + `reconcile materialize-edges --dsn`** — reads sharing-edge claims from
  the spine, runs the **P08.2** §29.3 reconciler (`reconcile.sharing.reconcile_sharing`, CONSUMED), and
  writes each reconciled directed access edge as an append-only, idempotent `relationship` row
  (insert-only; no UPDATE/DELETE; re-run +0). The three §12.2 access kinds stay strictly separate
  (SIG-ONTO-042); `edge_type = access_kind` (§12.5: access_kind is "which of the three edge types of
  §12.2"); every edge is evidenced (NOT-NULL `evidence_claim`, §3.1); asymmetry is RETURNED as a
  contradiction (kept VISIBLE, never reconciled away — materializing it is P28.3). Name-only partners
  (no `object_entity`) are reconciled but not materialized (no fabricated node). `read_materialized_edges`
  is the real edge dataset the P28.5 surface refresh (ADR-101) consumes.
- **`inference/access_paths.py` + `inference access-paths --dsn`** — `close_access_paths_over_spine`
  reads the materialized edges and derives bounded reachability closure via the **P12.2**
  `close_access_paths` (CONSUMED) — a labelled L4 inference (SIG-RECON-047) that feeds the web
  `access_paths` (empty until now). Layering respected: inference depends on reconcile, never the reverse.

## Design decisions

- **Reuse, not re-implement (SIG-ENG-035).** `reconcile_sharing` (§29.3) and `close_access_paths`
  (P12.2) are consumed verbatim; `reconcile.snapshot_diff` (§29.7) is untouched (owned/consumed at the
  connector layer). The materializer only reads claims, reconciles through the owned logic, and writes.
- **`edge_type = access_kind`.** §12.5 states `access_kind` is "which of the three edge types of §12.2";
  §12.9 speaks of "`configured_access` edges". The DB `edge_type` is free text (only `<> integrates_with`
  enforced). Documented in the module; no new ADR (posture is ADR-099/101).
- **Contradictions stay visible.** The reconciler's asymmetry findings are surfaced in the summary and
  both directed edges are kept; nothing is silently reconciled (P28.3 materializes contradiction rows).
